title: Risk and Insurance Stack for Pickleball Venues
one_liner: Incident logging, e-waivers, court-safety audits and an insurance program that make independent racquet venues insurable at fair prices.
customer: Independent indoor and outdoor pickleball and padel venue operators, plus HOAs and municipal recreation departments.
problem: Indoor pickleball operators report difficulty finding coverage, typical policies carry $1-5M general liability, injuries rose about 6.8x between 2017 and 2022, and noise disputes now end in lawsuits. Insurers lack venue-level data, so they price the category rather than the operator.
solution: Step one: $149-299 per month software with e-waivers, incident reporting, a photo-evidence court, lighting and fencing audit checklist and staff training. Step two: use the aggregated data to place operators with specialty carriers as a broker or MGA and negotiate premium credits for documented venues.
why_now: Venue counts have boomed while commentators now say the boom is starting to crack, which makes insurers and lenders demand evidence; no standard exists.
revenue_model: SaaS $149-299 per venue per month plus 10-15 percent broker or MGA commission on premiums of $8-30k per policy.
non_obvious_insight: Data is the product: when insurers lack venue-level evidence they price to the average, so the operator who documents beats the average. Start as software, then capture the insurance economics.
first_30_days: Partner with a licensed broker, audit 10 venues in one metro, produce an insurer-ready risk dossier for each, and take 20 dossiers to two specialty carriers.

title: Mod-Neutral Escrow for Reddit Swap Subs
one_liner: A roughly 2% escrow-and-reputation rail for r/hardwareswap-style trade communities that auto-writes verified trade counts, so buyers stop gambling on PayPal Goods & Services and mods stop refereeing scams.
customer: Buyers and sellers of $300-$5,000 used goods in Reddit trade subs (GPUs/RAM/SSDs, mechanical keyboards, watches, cameras, audio gear). Fee is split between both sides. Power traders and flippers are the first users because they feel chargeback pain most.
problem: Reddit's swap subs are unofficial high-ticket marketplaces run on mod-maintained 'confirmed trades' flair and PayPal G&S. Sellers get hit by chargebacks or 'not as described' reversals weeks later, even with signature confirmation. Buyers get hit by bogus-escrow scams and friends-and-family requests. Leaving for eBay costs about 13%, and PayPal G&S costs about 3.5% plus a fixed fee. Mods burn hours every week adjudicating disputes with no tooling. They also cannot endorse a paid vendor, because the Moderator Code of Conduct (Rule 5) bars compensation for moderation actions.
solution: Buyer funds are held through a licensed escrow partner. The seller ships with tracking, signature, and a serial-number photo checklist. Funds release after delivery plus a 72-hour inspection window. Disputes go to an evidence packet reviewed by a small paid panel of trusted high-volume traders. Every completed trade writes to a public read-only 'verified trades' API, plus a free Devvit flair-sync app any mod team can install to update trade counts automatically. Mods are never paid and the rail never touches moderation decisions.
why_now: The 2024-present global memory shortage has pushed RAM, SSD and GPU prices up several-fold, and a June 2026 class action alleges DRAM price fixing. That makes used-parts ticket sizes large enough that a 2% escrow fee is cheap insurance. Chargeback fraud on P2P payments is also a growing complaint among sellers.
revenue_model: 1.5-2.5% fee per side (undercutting PayPal G&S and eBay), optional insured-shipping add-on, and later a partner revenue share or float income on held funds. Enterprise-style deals with high-volume resellers who trade weekly.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is mod-trusted neutrality, not payments tech. Mods can't take money and won't bless a vendor who could be partial, so the winning rail is the one that is publicly documented, has zero mod financial relationship, and hands mods a free tool that deletes their number-one time sink (dispute refereeing and manual flair updates). Adoption is pulled by mod teams, not pushed by marketing. Serious traders also fear the 60-180 day chargeback tail more than the fee.
first_30_days: Sign with a licensed escrow or payments partner (an Escrow.com-style API, or Stripe Connect with held funds) so you avoid money-transmitter licensing. Start in one tight, high-ticket niche such as watches or keyboards rather than r/hardwareswap itself. Recruit 15 top-flair traders as design partners and waive fees on their first 30 trades. Build the Devvit flair-sync app and a public transparency page. Target about 200 escrowed trades at about $600 average, and track dispute rate and time-to-release as the proof points for mod teams.

title: Captive Insurer for Hardened Mountain Communities
one_liner: A group cell captive where associations with verified wildfire hardening share first-loss and reinsurance capital.
customer: Condo and townhome associations and mountain-resort communities in California and Colorado with $100K-$1M master premiums, plus their management companies.
problem: Master property premiums have exploded and carriers non-renew whole associations. Reinsurers hold record capital (about $790B, secondary source), yet cannot price unknown community-level risk. Rates fell up to 25% at June 1 2026, but retail carriers pass little through.
solution: A fronted group captive with quota-share reinsurance. Each association's mitigation (IBHS criteria, ember-resistant vents, vegetation plan) is verified and modeled with forward-looking cat models now allowed by California. Members keep the first-loss layer and share the dividends. The first product is captive feasibility plus a verified-hardening scorecard at $15-30K per association, which also improves standard-market placement.
why_now: Howden says reinsurer returns could fall below cost of capital by 2027, so reinsurers want differentiated, verified books now. California's Sustainable Insurance Strategy allows forward-looking models, and Colorado now credits mitigation.
revenue_model: Feasibility fees, then management fees of 8-12% of premium plus ceded profit commission.
non_obvious_insight: The soft reinsurance window is temporary and limited by data quality. Small verified pools can lock multi-year capacity before it hardens.
first_30_days: Meet 3 management companies, score 5 associations, and talk to fronting carriers and captive managers.

title: Grid-Paid Spiffs for Water Heater Installers
one_liner: Make the plumber on the emergency water-heater call the distribution channel for heat pump water heaters and grid demand-response programs, with a same-day rebate stack, an electrician handoff and a per-device bounty paid to the tech.
customer: Virtual power plant aggregators, utility demand-response and efficiency-program administrators and manufacturers' connected-water-heater programs, who pay for enrolled devices. The plumbing shop and tech are the paid channel partners.
problem: Roughly 9 million water heaters get replaced each year and the large majority are emergency replacements decided in a four-hour window, standing in an inch of water. The plumber decides what goes in. Utilities and aggregators spend hundreds of dollars per customer on mailers and rebates that almost nobody uses, because the customer does not think about the water heater until it dies. Plumbers install the 50-gallon tank on the truck because a heat pump unit needs a 240V circuit, a condensate drain, clearance and paperwork, plumbers do not do electrical, and a callback eats a week of margin. The federal 25C credit ended December 31, 2025, so what is left are state and utility rebates that customers cannot pre-approve while the old tank is leaking.
solution: An install-day tool for the tech's phone. Enter the ZIP, the current heater and a photo of the panel and get back every stackable rebate for that address with the homeowner's net cost against a like-for-like tank (a 20-second sales conversation). Route the 240V circuit to a pre-priced partner electrician for a next-day flat fee, or steer to a 120V plug-in heat pump model when the panel is tight. At install, scan the QR on the heater to enroll it in the aggregator or utility program with the customer's consent. Pay the tech a same-week spiff and the shop a fee. We handle rebate paperwork in the background so the plumber's job ends when the tank is set.
why_now: Federal tax credits are gone, so utility and state programs and point-of-sale rebates now decide the price difference. Virtual power plants and utility demand-response are actively looking for cheap, high-volume device enrollment. Manufacturers now ship connected and 120V plug-in heat pump units that remove the biggest install objections. The labor-constrained plumber has never been offered a spiff that is bigger than the hassle.
revenue_model: Take 20-30% of the per-device enrollment or midstream incentive paid by the aggregator or utility (typically $200-600 per device is now spent on customer acquisition), pay $50-100 to the tech and $50-100 to the shop, and keep the rest. Add a per-install electrician referral fee and a $99 per month shop subscription for the rebate engine once volumes justify it.
non_obvious_insight: The whole electrification industry markets to homeowners, who make no decision until the tank fails. The only person who actually decides is a plumber with a 20-minute window, paid by the ticket and hating callbacks. Plumbers will not sell a heat pump water heater because it is a worse day for them, not because they are anti-green. Fix the day and the channel opens, and the spiff is the cheapest customer acquisition the grid will ever buy.
first_30_days: Choose one territory with a live heat pump water heater rebate plus a demand-response or VPP program (e.g. Massachusetts, Colorado, the Pacific Northwest or California). Build the rebate stack for that utility in a spreadsheet and a text-message enrollment link. Sign 5 shops and 1 partner electrician. Pitch an aggregator or the program administrator a pilot of 100 enrolled devices at an agreed bounty, with the spiff paid manually at first.

title: Belonging Pods to Cut Home-Care Aide Turnover
one_liner: Weekly peer pods and buddy mentors for isolated home-care aides, sold to agencies as a turnover-reduction service priced per retained aide.
customer: Home-care agencies (tens of thousands in the US, 50-500 aides each) and the Medicaid managed-care and Medicare Advantage plans that fund them, paying $8-15 per aide per month.
problem: Aides work alone in strangers' homes, with annual turnover often 65-80% and a replacement cost of several thousand dollars each. Engagement surveys measure isolation but fix nothing. Clients die and aides grieve without support. The workforce hired to cure elder loneliness is itself lonely, and agencies experience the pain only as attrition.
solution: Pods of 6 aides grouped by geography and shift, with a weekly 30-minute voice huddle (dial-in works, no app needed), a paid peer mentor per 30 aides, a monthly in-person meal, a 'hard visit' debrief line, and scripts for client death. A dashboard shows pod attendance against 90-day retention for the agency.
why_now: The aide shortage is acute. Immigration enforcement in 2025-26 is reported to be thinning a workforce in which roughly a quarter are immigrants. Plans and agencies want cheap retention levers, and loneliness is now legitimized as a health metric.
revenue_model: Per-aide monthly subscription with a performance kicker tied to retention, plus facilitator staffing margin. Later contracts with managed-care plans.
non_obvious_insight: Agencies do not buy belonging, they buy retention. Framing belonging as a turnover product with a hard ROI (each retained aide saves thousands) unlocks a budget that wellness and loneliness framing never will.
first_30_days: Sign three agencies with 100+ aides through state home-care association chapters. Run pods for about 60 aides and compare 90-day retention against a control group. Charge $6 per aide per month for the pilot.

title: Robotic Pack-to-Cell Teardown for E-Bike Fleets
one_liner: A robot cell driven by a vision-language-action model that opens e-bike and scooter packs, tests every cell, and regrades them for low-cost storage.
customer: Delivery-app fleet operators, e-bike and scooter share operators, battery-swap networks and repair shops (pay per pack), with buyers of graded cells for stationary storage.
problem: Micromobility packs are the high-volume end-of-life lithium stream arriving now, while EV end-of-life will not dominate until after 2040. Manual teardown is dangerous and slow, so packs go to shredders at low value or sit in shops as fire risks.
solution: A cell with a robot foundation model fine-tuned on pack disassembly with force feedback. It cuts nickel strips, pulls cells, tests each one (IR and impedance), grades A/B/C, and repackages A-grade cells for stationary storage or tools. C-grade goes to recyclers. It starts as a manual-plus-robotic service in one city.
why_now: 2025-26 robot foundation models made unstructured manipulation tasks feasible, and e-bike fire scrutiny gives fleets a reason to pay.
revenue_model: Fee per pack processed, plus margin on graded cells, plus recycler payments for C-grade.
non_obvious_insight: Recyclers built for EV packs face feed that is 15 years late. E-bike packs are small enough that a robot cell amortizes quickly, and their cells are far from dead.
first_30_days: Contract with 2 fleet operators or a swap network in NYC or LA. Rent a bench with a fire-safe enclosure and cell testers. Process 500 packs manually to build the dataset and unit economics before adding the robot.

title: Hospital-Guaranteed Loans for Excluded Health Programs
one_liner: Employer-cosigned, service-obligation tuition loans for nursing, OT, PT and counseling students that the new federal caps abandoned.
customer: Hospital systems, rural health networks, behavioral-health agencies and skilled-nursing chains (they guarantee or buy down); their incoming students and employees; a CDFI or specialty-finance fund as capital partner.
problem: Since July 1, 2026 Grad PLUS is gone, grad loans are capped at $20.5k per year and $100k total, and nursing, OT, PT, counseling, psychology and social work were excluded from the higher 'professional' cap. Private lenders are tightening, and predatory loans run up to 16% APR. These fields face the most AI-resistant shortages, including nurse educators, NPs and therapists.
solution: A loan product with employer guarantee or interest buy-down, a 2-3 year service commitment, and retention-linked forgiveness paid by the employer as tenure accrues. Underwrite on licensure pass rates and a signed job offer rather than FICO. The employer gets a cheaper pipeline and retention tool than agency staffing or sign-on bonuses.
why_now: The cap regime took effect in July 2026. A healthcare-association lawsuit is pending, with a December 2026 suspension deadline, so uncertainty is high. Incumbent lenders are retreating. Hospitals are under labor-cost pressure.
revenue_model: 2-3% origination fee, servicing spread, and a per-participant employer program fee. Use a bank-partner or licensed-lender model at first so you don't need your own lending licenses.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders read the cap as proof these programs are too risky to finance. In fact, licensure-gated wages and very high employment make them among the best credits in higher ed. The natural underwriter is not a bank but the employer who would otherwise pay a large premium for temporary staff.
first_30_days: Pick one state and 2 hospital systems that already run tuition assistance. Pitch a $2M pilot warehouse line from a CDFI or hospital foundation for about 20 students starting January 2027. Engage a licensed bank or lender partner and counsel on structure.

title: Launch and Reentry Airspace Forecasts for Airlines
one_liner: A dispatcher-facing forecast of whether launch and debris closures will really happen, and what rerouting will cost.
customer: Airline operations control centers on Caribbean, Atlantic and Pacific routes, cargo airlines, business-jet operators and flight-planning software vendors.
problem: Launches hit 321 in 2025, and Starship debris in early 2025 disrupted flights around Florida and the Caribbean. Launch slips and scrubs make late notices unreliable. Dispatchers over-buffer fuel and time or get surprised, and there is no probabilistic view of hazard areas.
solution: An API and dashboard that fuses launch manifests, vehicle-specific slip and scrub statistics, trajectory and debris-response-area models, and reentry predictions. It outputs closure probability and expected reroute cost per flight. Deliver it into existing flight-planning tools as a plug-in.
why_now: Cadence is climbing (223 launches in 2023 to 321 in 2025), Starship is flying orbital profiles, and new vehicles such as New Glenn and Stoke's Nova are coming. Airspace impact scales with cadence.
revenue_model: $30-150k per year per airline. Per-flight API fees through flight-planning vendors. Cargo and charter tiers.
non_obvious_insight: The valuable prediction is not where the hazard area is but whether the launch will actually go, which is a schedule-slip model. That converts publicly available manifests into a decision-quality product.
first_30_days: Backtest a slip and scrub model on the last 12 months of Florida and Vandenberg launches. Show it to five dispatch managers at airlines flying Caribbean routes. Offer a free pilot on one route and a paid tier for the next quarter.

title: Billable Legacy Circles for Advance Care Planning
one_liner: Community 'legacy circles' where older adults tell their life stories and finish their advance directives, with a clinician in the room to bill the Medicare advance-care-planning visit.
customer: Medicare Advantage plans and ACOs chasing advance-care-planning quality measures (paying per completed and documented ACP), plus adults 60+ paying about $79-99 for the circle and a keepsake legacy book.
problem: The longevity industry sells more years but says nothing about what they are for, while the 65+ population is peaking and lonely. Advance care planning has had Medicare billing codes for years (99497/99498), yet few eligible people have one, because it is framed as paperwork about death and clinicians have no time. The meaning conversation people actually want is unbilled, and the billable one is avoided.
solution: A 4-session circle of 6-8 people in libraries, churches and senior centers covers values, life story (dignity-therapy style prompts) and what a good ending looks like. Each participant then has a 30-minute individual ACP visit with an NP or social worker under a billing clinician, who files the health-care proxy or POLST. AI transcription and editing produce a 'legacy book' or short video for family. Plans get documented ACPs and engagement data, and participants get a keepsake and a group of peers.
why_now: About 4M Americans turn 65 each year through 2027, so demand is at a peak. Advantage plans are under margin and Star-rating pressure and want cheap, measurable gap-closing. AI transcription and editing make personalized legacy artifacts cheap. Longevity and GLP-1 hype have surfaced the 'healthspan for what' question.
revenue_model: ACP visit billing (about $85-100 per 99497 under Medicare), per-completion fees from MA plans and ACOs, $79-99 participant fee for the circle and legacy book, and sponsorship by estate-planning and elder-law firms.
non_obvious_insight: Advance care planning fails because it is sold as death admin and done alone. Framed as a legacy-building group with a keepsake, participants pull themselves in. The billing code is the boring spine that lets a community and meaning program be paid by a health plan. The group covers the reflection, and the individual visit, not the group, is what gets billed.
first_30_days: Recruit one NP or LCSW (with a supervising physician) and two host venues, such as a public library and a church. Run three circles at $79 and produce sample legacy books. Take the results to the quality lead of one MA plan or ACO that publishes an ACP gap list. Confirm payer-specific billing rules with a compliance advisor before billing anything.

title: Slop-Rating Feed for Kids' Filters
one_liner: A channel- and app-level data feed that classifies children's content as verified human-made, AI slop or unknown, sold to school web filters and kids' hardware.
customer: School-district web-filter and parental-control vendors, kids' tablet, audio-player and smart-speaker makers, and school districts directly.
problem: Fairplay found that 104 of the first 500 videos recommended to a fresh account were AI slop. On 1 Apr 2026 more than 200 organisations, including the American Federation of Teachers, asked YouTube to label and ban AI content on kids' surfaces, and YouTube said only that it is developing labels. Filters classify by topic (violence, adult), not by how content was produced.
solution: Continuously crawl kids-targeted channels, apps, audiobooks and games. Classify provenance using channel behaviour, voice and image-model signals, upload cadence and template reuse, plus human review. Add a 'verified human-made' tier through creator attestations and audits. Deliver category lists by API keyed on channel ID, domain or app package, plus teacher whitelist packs.
why_now: Spring 2026 investigations (NYT, Fairplay, CBC) and the April coalition letter made AI slop a school and parent issue. The EU AI Act's Article 50 labelling is beginning, and 1:1 school device fleets need a new filter category now.
revenue_model: $20-200k per year data licences to filter vendors, $0.10-0.50 per-device royalties from hardware makers, and $1-3 per student per year for districts.
non_obvious_insight: A platform's own AI label will always be optional and gameable. The buyer is whoever sits between the child and the platform, and they already buy category feeds. Selling a new dimension (provenance) into an existing distribution channel avoids consumer acquisition entirely.
first_30_days: Build a 20k-channel labelled seed set with three teacher or parent reviewers. Ship a free 'slop score' browser extension for teachers to collect signals and leads. Pitch three mid-size filter and parental-control vendors with a sample feed.

title: Passive-Radar Drone Detection for Prisons
one_liner: Detect small drones by listening to ambient cell, broadcast and Wi-Fi signals, with no transmitter, no license and no radar permit.
customer: State departments of corrections, county jails, and secondary customers such as critical infrastructure and stadiums.
problem: Cape Canaveral radars see aircraft up to a 747 but not a quadcopter. State prisons face contraband drops with low budgets and cannot deploy active radar or jammers. Remote ID and RF detection miss drones that are not broadcasting.
solution: A rooftop kit of low-cost software-defined radios using the signal reflections of existing cell towers and broadcast transmitters, with ML-based detection of small-drone Doppler signatures. It alerts a mobile app and logs evidence for prosecution, and it is passive so legal risk is minimal.
why_now: Cheap SDRs and modern ML make passive sensing of low-cross-section targets feasible in 2025-26. Small-drone detection is now flagged as thin even at major federal sites, and drone traffic is exploding with 200,000-unit purchases (verify feasibility and prison contraband scale).
revenue_model: $25-60K per site installation plus $500-1,500 per month for software and monitoring.
non_obvious_insight: Passivity is the business model. Local agencies cannot legally emit RF or mitigate, so a purely receiving sensor is the only kind they can buy without federal permission.
first_30_days: Recruit one university RF lab. Pilot on a rooftop with an existing tower nearby and log real drone passes. Approach 3 state corrections security chiefs for a paid pilot.

title: Tip Passport: Mortgage-Ready Records for Tipped Workers
one_liner: An app that logs every cash and card tip in a lender-grade ledger so young bartenders, stylists, servers and valets can claim the new tip deduction and finally qualify for a mortgage or lease.
customer: Gen Z and young-millennial tipped workers (servers, bartenders, hair and nail techs, barbers, delivery and other occupations on the IRS list) earning $50-$120k with largely undocumented cash tips. Lenders and landlords pay for verified income.
problem: Cash tips have long been under-reported to avoid tax, so returns show low income and lenders qualify people on returns and W-2s. A stylist netting $90k cannot get a mortgage. The new deduction of up to $25,000 in qualified tips makes reporting valuable, but workers have no system, fear audits, and employer POS captures only card tips.
solution: One-tap, voice and QR tip logging with imports from Venmo, Cash App and POS. It produces monthly tip statements in IRS-recognized format, a deduction-ready schedule, a tax-reserve estimate and a 'lender pack' with 24-month income narrative reconciled to bank deposits. The pack is accepted by partner bank-statement lenders and landlords. Built-in classification excludes service charges and mandatory gratuities that do not qualify.
why_now: Final regulations (TD 10044) published April 13, 2026 confirm the 70+ qualifying occupations for the deduction on tips received in 2025-2028. 2026 is the first year workers can plan around it. The sunset after 2028 creates a roughly two-year window to build the 24-month record lenders want, and non-QM bank-statement lending is available.
revenue_model: $8-$12 per month or $79 per year, a lender referral fee of $300-$1,500 per funded loan, $25 per landlord verification report, and a B2B retention perk sold to salon suites and restaurant groups.
non_obvious_insight: A tax incentive flips the incentive from hiding income to documenting it for the first time in decades, and the same document (proof of income) is worth ten times the tax savings because it unlocks a mortgage. The moat is trusted, lender-accepted record-keeping, not tax prep.
first_30_days: Find 100 stylists and bartenders through salon-suite communities and beauty and hospitality creators on social media. Sell a tip ledger plus deduction estimate at $9 per month. Partner with one bank-statement lender and one CPA who signs off on the statement format. Track pre-approvals within 90 days as the proof point.

title: Independent Battery Safety Review for Counties
one_liner: Sell counties and fire marshals a developer-funded third-party plan review, hazard analysis and first-responder plan for every battery project.
customer: Storage developers pay the fees, usually through a county-controlled escrow. Counties and fire authorities contract the reviewer, and insurers use the dossiers.
problem: US storage installs hit a record 18.9 GWh in Q2 2026. After the January 2025 Moss Landing fire, hearings turn hostile and local moratoria spread. Fire departments lack expertise, NFPA 855 and UL 9540A data are hard to interpret, and developers lose 6-12 months in permitting.
solution: An independent safety dossier: hazard mitigation analysis, interpretation of large-scale fire test data, an emergency response plan, a thermal and off-gas monitoring plan and training for local responders. Sell it as fixed-price packages with an annual inspection option, plus a model county ordinance and review checklist.
why_now: Record installs are moving into populated areas, moratoria and insurer repricing are active, and code cycles are updating.
revenue_model: $25-80k per project via the county escrow, $5-10k a year for inspections, and training contracts.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is trust, not technology. A reviewer the county chooses but the developer pays, like a planning consultant, speeds approvals and removes the NIMBY veto.
first_30_days: Draft a model BESS review ordinance and checklist. Offer free reviews to three counties with pending applications. Get two developers to pay for pre-application dossiers. Retain a fire-protection PE and a retired fire marshal.

title: Care-First Reverse Mortgages With Locked Payouts
one_liner: A care-planning broker that funds long-term care from home equity and releases the money only to verified caregivers and facilities.
customer: Homeowners 70-85 with $300k+ equity and thin liquid savings, or their adult children holding a power of attorney. The channel is elder-law attorneys, geriatric care managers and hospital discharge planners.
problem: Long-term-care insurance is failing policyholders: Genworth has about $31.8B of approved premium hikes, and 2023 hikes averaged 51%. Care runs $75-115k a year, and Medicaid retrenchment is coming. The one big asset is home equity, but advisors still treat reverse mortgages as a last resort and lump sums invite fraud and sibling fights.
solution: Start with a 12-month care budget and plan. Match it to a reverse-mortgage line of credit (HECM or proprietary), through an NMLS-licensed broker or a co-brokering partner. Then open a care wallet: funds go only to vetted payees (agency, facility, or a family caregiver under a documented personal-care agreement with payroll), with a ledger for siblings and Medicaid look-back records, and multi-party approval for any other outflow.
why_now: Proprietary reverse mortgages now hold 52% share against 48% for HECM, so products are better. Seniors hold $14.92T in home equity. LTC insurance is unravelling, the 80+ cohort is exploding, and elder fraud hit $7.7B in 2025 (up 59%), which makes lump-sum liquidity risky without controls.
revenue_model: Broker origination compensation on funded loans, roughly 1-2% of loan amount, plus a $49 a month care-wallet fee. Licensing the wallet to lenders as a fraud-protection differentiator is later upside.
non_obvious_insight: The product isn't the loan; it's controlled disbursement plus a care plan. Reverse mortgages are viewed with suspicion because of how the cash gets spent, and a locked, audited payout stream fixes the exact failure mode that ruined the category's reputation.
first_30_days: Partner with a licensed reverse-mortgage broker, publish 'how to pay for care with home equity' content, and build referral relationships with 10 elder-law firms and care managers. Loans close in about 60-75 days, so first revenue lands inside six months.

title: GST Credit Recovery on UPI Fees
one_liner: Recover the 18% GST on new UPI MDR fees as input credit for retailers and distributors that will otherwise never claim it.
customer: GST-registered mobile, FMCG and pharma retailers and distributors in India, and their chartered accountants.
problem: From Oct 15 the 0.4% MDR carries 18% GST, and AICPDF estimates a Rs 7,000-9,000 Cr burden on distributors. Small businesses will not reconcile bulk PSP fee invoices to GSTR-2B, so credit is left unclaimed.
solution: Ingest PSP settlement reports, match fee invoices to GSTR-2B, flag missing credits and produce claim workpapers for CAs. Composition-scheme dealers are ineligible and must be screened out. The wedge is retailer associations already mobilising over the fee.
why_now: MDR starts Oct 15 and retailer bodies are organised around a 'No UPI Day' on Oct 2.
revenue_model: 10-15% of recovered credit, or Rs 499-1,999 per month per business.
non_obvious_insight: The protest is about the 0.4%. The GST layer is partly recoverable money nobody is discussing, and associations will trade it for a visible win for members.
first_30_days: Build reconciliation for PhonePe and Paytm settlement file formats and sign two retailer associations.

title: A Marketplace for Canal Capacity, Not Water
one_liner: A scheduling and capacity-release board that lets irrigation districts sell idle canal and wheeling capacity so conserved or recharge water can physically move to buyers.
customer: Irrigation districts and mutual ditch companies with spare conveyance capacity (sellers), plus growers, groundwater agencies, cities and conservation buyers who need water moved (buyers). Districts pay a subscription and buyers pay per acre-foot wheeled.
problem: Everyone is building marketplaces for water rights and acre-feet. In Western practice the binding constraint is often the ability and permission to move water: capacity, wheeling agreements, losses, turnout scheduling. Idle capacity sits unused while buyers cannot get water delivered. Districts handle wheeling requests by phone and spreadsheet.
solution: Wedge: a shared capacity calendar and wheeling-request workflow for districts, with loss accounting and standard agreements. Then a capacity-release market, like the gas-pipeline capacity release model. The ditch-company share ledger (shares, assessments, transfer approvals) is phase two. Start with one region where transfers already happen.
why_now: The 2027-2036 Colorado River framework and corporate buyers like Amazon create conserved water that must be moved. California groundwater rules and canal capacity loss to subsidence make wheeling scarce. Cheap LoRa gate sensors and open flow gauges make district digitization affordable.
revenue_model: $10-40k/yr district SaaS, plus $5-15 per acre-foot wheeled (roughly 3-5% of price).
non_obvious_insight: Price discovery is missing for the pipes, not the water. Whoever runs the capacity ledger sees every buyer, seller and route, and that data is the moat for every later water market product.
first_30_days: Interview 10 district managers and ditch riders and find one that handles recurring wheeling requests manually. Ship a free shared calendar and request workflow to that district using off-the-shelf tools. Agree that the district will pay per wheeled acre-foot at season end. Publish a public canal-capacity map from open gauge data as top-of-funnel.

title: Fees-in-Kind: Harvest Becomes School Fee Credit
one_liner: A weigh-in and ledger service that lets parents pay school fees with maize, beans and potatoes at a transparent price, while schools get cheaper, steadier food supply.
customer: Boards of management, principals and bursars of public boarding and day secondary schools, including the new senior-school cohorts, plus rural private schools. The end users are smallholder parents in maize, bean and potato zones.
problem: Farm households are asset-rich and cash-poor exactly when fees fall due in January, May and August. Schools already accept 'a tin of maize' informally, but the value is whatever the storekeeper or bursar decides, with no receipts. Meanwhile the same schools buy food through brokers at inflated tender prices, and government capitation often arrives late. Children still get sent home over arrears even when the parents' store is full of grain. Food is often the largest line in a boarding school's budget.
solution: A Fee Credit Ledger. Farmers deliver graded produce to the school store or a village collection point. A standard weigh ticket (photo of the scale plus a moisture reading) generates an SMS receipt, and the value is credited to the learner's fee account at a published reference price such as NCPB or the county market average, minus a small handling margin. The school gets a weekly reconciliation. On the buying side, the platform, registered as an AGPO-eligible youth or women group (check how each school's procurement committee applies the 30% reservation), bids for school food supply and sources from the same parents. It pools, grades and quality-checks (moisture, aflatoxin spot test). An add-on is hermetic storage bags on credit so parents can deliver later in the term rather than dumping at harvest.
why_now: The first CBC cohort entered senior school in January 2026, expanding boarding and food demand, and the next cohort arrives in January 2027, so schools are planning Term 1 supply now. Capitation delays keep squeezing school food budgets. Cheap Bluetooth scales, moisture meters and M-Pesa and SMS receipts make a trustworthy weigh ticket trivial. Principals in Kenya talk in tight associations, so one working pilot spreads fast.
revenue_model: A 4-8% handling margin on food flow: schools pay below their current broker-inclusive price and farmers receive above the broker price. Later a per-learner per-term ledger fee (about KES 50-100). Once the ledger produces credit-quality data, short-term financing of fee arrears or school receivables.
non_obvious_insight: In every rural ward the school is the largest, most predictable institutional food buyer, and the 'fee arrears list' is a timing and valuation mismatch, not poverty. Fintechs treat barter as embarrassing or informal, but for smallholders paying in maize is the default. What is missing is fair valuation and a ledger everyone trusts. The AGPO set-aside is an under-used entry ticket for farmer groups into school tenders.
first_30_days: Sign 2-3 principals through your own old high school or a heads' association branch meeting for a one-term pilot in January 2027. Buy two Bluetooth hanging scales and moisture meters (a few hundred dollars), run the ledger on Google Sheets plus Africa's Talking SMS, and recruit 100 parent households at PTA meetings. Set the price at the midpoint between the farmgate broker price and the school tender price. Register the entity for AGPO and open a supplier profile with the school.

title: Drone Hub Siting and Permit Intelligence
one_liner: Parcel-level zoning, noise and neighbor-risk scoring, plus done-for-you permit filing, for retailers and drone operators expanding launch hubs.
customer: Real-estate and expansion teams at retailers (Walmart, Lowe's, grocers, pharmacies), drone operators and delivery platforms such as Wing, Zipline and DoorDash, and regional chains entering drone delivery.
problem: Cities cannot regulate flight paths but can regulate launch hubs. Northglenn, for example, requires a special-use permit, a 200 ft residential buffer and no more than 65 dB at the property line. Walmart and Wing plan 270+ sites by 2027 (about 150 stores added in a year), and each is a separate local land-use fight.
solution: An LLM-parsed database of municipal zoning codes and drone ordinances, an acoustic model of hub operations, and parcel scoring (buffer, noise, neighbor density, HOA covenants) that outputs a go/no-go and a permit dossier. Add concierge filing and hearing prep. Also sell a model-ordinance toolkit to city planners.
why_now: Lowe's launched Wing/DoorDash delivery on September 28, 2026, and Walmart's rollout turns hub siting into a mass-production problem. With airspace approvals no longer the binding constraint, zoning boards are. LLMs make parsing thousands of local codes cheap.
revenue_model: $2-5k per site score, $10-25k per permit package, and $50-150k a year in enterprise SaaS. City licenses for the planning toolkit are a smaller add-on.
non_obvious_insight: The sky is federally preempted but the ground is local, so the scaling constraint has moved from the FAA to the zoning board. Whoever owns the ordinance graph decides where drone networks can expand, and both sides of the table will pay.
first_30_days: Scrape and structure drone-relevant ordinances for the top 150 municipalities in one high-growth state. Offer a free top-20 site scoring to a regional grocery or pharmacy chain, convert one paid permit package, and publish a model ordinance to generate city leads.

title: License-in-a-Box for Insourcing Property Owners
one_liner: A licensed managing-broker entity, trust-account oversight and compliance layer that lets owners run AI-native property management in-house without building licensing state by state.
customer: Institutional owners, family offices, search-fund operators and AI-native property-ops startups with 500-10,000 units that want to insource management.
problem: Owners are insourcing to capture AI efficiency and stop paying a percentage-of-rent fee (T2 Capital's Base Living launched with 24 site associates and 8 corporate staff across three states). Most states require a licensed broker of record, trust accounts, fair-housing controls and E&O cover, and each new state costs months of licensing and hires.
solution: A licensed entity in 20+ states supervises the owner's own operation: trust-accounting oversight integrated with Yardi, AppFolio and Entrata, monthly reconciliations, fair-housing and fee-law compliance, E&O coverage and regulator liaison. Owners run day-to-day operations with their own AI stack.
why_now: The insourcing wave is underway, third-party manager incentives are misaligned, and the fee and pricing-law patchwork is raising compliance load.
revenue_model: $1.50-3.50 per unit per month plus a $10-25K onboarding fee per state, and an E&O program revenue share.
non_obvious_insight: The barrier to AI-native operations is not software but a licensed human of record in every state, which is cheap to rent and expensive to build. Incumbent managers will not sell it because it undermines their fee model.
first_30_days: Form the entity with a multi-state-licensed broker and counsel. Sign two owners with 500-2,000 units in one or two states as reduced-rate design partners. Get an E&O quote and publish a free state-by-state licensing matrix as a lead magnet.

title: Dialysis Chair-Fill Rides Paid Per Completed Treatment
one_liner: A dedicated, route-based ride service for dialysis patients (same driver, same van loop, three times a week) priced per treatment completed instead of per trip, sold to the clinics and risk-bearing kidney-care companies that lose money on every missed session.
customer: Independent dialysis clinic groups and mid-sized operators worried about chair utilization, plus value-based kidney-care companies and Medicare Advantage ESRD plans that carry the hospitalization cost when a patient misses treatment.
problem: Medicaid non-emergency transport is a low-margin, hated business: pooled dispatch, late or missed pickups, and one-off rides for patients who actually have 156 predictable trips a year. The largest broker, ModivCare, went through Chapter 11 in 2025, so states and payers are unhappy with the incumbent. Meanwhile a missed dialysis session is expensive: in one study about 5% of patients were hospitalized within two days of a missed appointment versus 1.2% of those who attended. Medicare pays the clinic a bundled rate of about $282 per treatment in 2026, so every no-show is lost revenue, an idle chair and staff, and a sicker patient.
solution: Run dialysis like a bus route. Batch patients by chair shift and neighborhood, fix pickup windows, and assign dedicated driver-and-vehicle pairs so the patient sees the same person every time. Add SMS check-in, a same-day fallback ride through a taxi or rideshare partner, and a no-show guarantee. Report completed-treatment rates to the clinic weekly. Price by completed treatment (a round trip in the tens of dollars against roughly $280 of chair revenue), with an upside share for a lower missed-session rate. Structure it inside the Anti-Kickback local-transportation safe harbor, or bill risk-bearing plans and kidney-care companies directly, and confirm that with health-care counsel before launch.
why_now: ModivCare's bankruptcy and its emergence at the end of 2025 left NEMT contracts in flux and states re-examining brokers. CMS's kidney care models and Medicare Advantage special-needs plans are pushing risk onto companies that now feel every hospital day. Federal Medicaid cuts mean clinics and plans need cheaper ways to protect revenue rather than more benefits.
revenue_model: Fee per completed treatment (about $45-$75 round trip depending on wheelchair mix), with a bonus tied to reducing the clinic's missed-treatment rate. Second line: chemo and radiation patients on the same route logic.
non_obvious_insight: A dialysis chair is perishable inventory, like an airline seat, and the ride is a $50 cost that protects a $280 seat-day and a threefold hospitalization risk. NEMT is a terrible business because it treats a predictable, recurring, high-stakes patient as a random one-off trip. Treat those patients as a subscription route and the economics flip from a race to the bottom on price per mile to a premium on reliability.
first_30_days: Sell one independent operator with 3-5 clinics in one metro on a 60-day pilot covering 15-20 patients. Use two leased accessible vans, or subcontract a local NEMT operator, and two salaried drivers. Get the clinic's baseline missed-treatment rate from its own records and agree the target in writing before starting. Charge per completed treatment from day one, then take the data to a kidney-care company or MA plan for a larger contract.

title: Grid-Code Models for AI Data Centers
one_liner: Validated dynamic load models and ride-through test packages so data centers can pass the same grid-code exams that generators pass.
customer: Interconnection teams at hyperscalers, neoclouds and colo developers, and their EPCs. Transmission owners and ISOs need the models validated, and the developer pays.
problem: About 1.5 GW of Northern Virginia data center load tripped offline together during a 2024 fault. AI training loads swing tens of MW in seconds, and xAI buys Megapacks largely to smooth them. Texas SB 6 and NERC large-load work now push for ride-through and dynamic models, but no standard model library or test lab exists for GPU cluster, power-supply and UPS stacks.
solution: Build a parametric EMT and PSS/E model library for common facility architectures (UPS topologies, PSU behavior, 800V DC). Validate it with hardware-in-the-loop tests at a partner lab. Sell per-project model packages, ride-through study reports and compliance-ready certification letters. Charge a subscription to keep models current as hardware changes.
why_now: Multi-GW campuses, NERC's large-load task force and Texas and PJM interconnection rules in 2025-26 are turning load models from optional into a gating item.
revenue_model: $75-300k per project for the model and study, an annual model-maintenance subscription, and test or certification fees paid by UPS and power-shelf OEMs.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone frames data centers as demand. The grid now treats them as a dynamic device, like a giant inverter-based generator. Inverter-generator modeling became a consulting industry after events like the 2016 Blue Cut fire, and large-load modeling will follow. The model library is the moat.
first_30_days: Recruit one or two power-electronics engineers from a utility or ISO. Publish an open primer on GPU-load oscillation. Contact interconnection leads at 10 neoclouds and 5 TO planners. Sell a $15k 'large-load model gap analysis'. Sign a university hardware-in-the-loop lab as a partner.

title: Buildings-as-Mines Salvage Reserve Reports
one_liner: Mining-style reserve estimates for buildings before demolition, built from phone LiDAR and AI that reads the drawings, then a market for pre-sold salvage rights.
customer: Demolition and selective-strip contractors and developers doing office-to-residential conversions (first), later scrap buyers, banks and salvors.
problem: Demolition bids depend on a walk-through guess of salvage value in copper, aluminum, steel, glass and fixtures. Contractors overpay or underbid, and no one sells forward the metals inside a building, unlike any mined commodity.
solution: A 48-hour reserve report with tonnage, value and confidence bands (P10/P50/P90). It uses LiDAR and thermal scans, stud and cable finders, and an LLM that reads as-builts and MEP drawings. A bid-day marketplace lets salvage buyers commit. Long term, salvage-rights forwards on the building stock.
why_now: Phone LiDAR and models that can read drawings became good enough in 2025-26, at a time when office conversions are surging and metal prices are elevated.
revenue_model: $1.5-5K per report, plus 3-5% of salvage value transacted through the marketplace.
non_obvious_insight: Demolition is the only mining-like business with no reserve estimate. Once a reserve report exists, salvage rights become financeable and pre-sellable.
first_30_days: Scan 10 buildings free with a partner contractor, then back-test estimates against actual scale tickets. Sell the first reports at $1,500 to 5 contractors.

title: Practice-in-a-Box for Licensed Paraprofessionals
one_liner: Turn displaced paralegals into licensed legal paraprofessionals who can legally sell AI-leveraged flat-fee services directly to the public in states that now allow it.
customer: Displaced or at-risk paralegals and legal assistants, paying $149-299/month, who serve consumers with family law, landlord-tenant, and limited civil matters in states with limited-license programs (Arizona LP, Utah LPP, Oregon LP, Colorado LLP, Minnesota developing).
problem: AI has pushed the value of routine paralegal tasks toward zero inside law firms, while most low-income people's legal problems get little or no help. Several states created limited licenses for exactly this gap, but the licensed pool is tiny because the path (exams, supervised hours, malpractice insurance, trust accounting, client acquisition, tooling) is costly and lonely for a laid-off individual.
solution: A 'practice in a box' with exam and supervised-hours prep, a group malpractice policy, compliant trust accounting, standard intake and scope-check forms, an AI drafting stack with mandatory citation verification and human sign-off, and shared consumer marketing for flat-fee packages (for example, $900 uncontested divorce). It hands off cleanly to lawyers when a matter is out of scope. To respect fee-sharing rules, the company charges flat subscription fees, never a percentage of legal fees.
why_now: Entry-level paralegal roles are among the most cited casualties of 2026 AI layoffs. Colorado's LLP program launched in 2024, Arizona's has licensed since 2021, and Oregon approved its license in 2022. AI drafting makes flat-fee economics finally work for a solo practitioner.
revenue_model: $149-299/month practitioner subscription, exam-prep courses (about $600), group insurance commissions, and per-practitioner advertising placements where permitted.
non_obvious_insight: When AI drives the cost of doing legal work to near zero, the scarce asset is the license to sell it. Regulators created cheap licenses for access-to-justice reasons and they sit underused. Displaced paralegals are the natural supply. The moat is regulatory and operational, not technological.
first_30_days: Pick Arizona and Colorado. Recruit 15 laid-off paralegals through paralegal associations and LinkedIn. Sign a malpractice broker. Launch a $49 'is my matter in scope?' consumer screen as lead generation. Sell exam-prep and onboarding to the first 10 practitioners, about $2k in monthly recurring revenue plus course fees.

title: Customs Broker-as-Software for LatAm Micro-Importers
one_liner: Tariff walls turn Temu-era resellers into importers, so sell them classification, duty prepayment and pre-filed declarations.
customer: Parcel consolidators and micro-importers in Mexico and Argentina, and courier forwarders serving them.
problem: Temu has 105M LatAm monthly users, Mexico charges 33.5% on parcels and Argentina proposes a 30% duty. Resellers now face classification, valuation and tax questions, and brokers charge per-entry fees that kill small shipments.
solution: An HS-code classifier, duty calculator, pre-filed declaration flow and duty prepayment float. The wedge is consolidators shipping 200-1,000 parcels a week from China.
why_now: Anti-parcel walls went up across LatAm in 2025-26, and Indonesia's de minimis cut shows the pattern spreading.
revenue_model: $2-5 per parcel plus 1-2% on duty financing.
non_obvious_insight: Tariff walls do not kill cross-border demand, they create a compliance tax, and the seller of compliance wins on volume.
first_30_days: Partner with two forwarders and cover the 20 most common HS codes for their volume.

title: Age-Tier Compliance for Roblox-Style Creator Studios
one_liner: Pre-flight scanner and consulting that checks user-generated game experiences against Roblox Kids (<9), Select (9-15) and 16+ tier rules before discovery demotion costs revenue.
customer: UGC studios and creators earning $200k-$10M a year on Roblox and similar platforms (Fortnite UEFN), plus brand agencies commissioning sponsored experiences.
problem: Roblox mandated age checks (Jan 2026) and split into Kids, Select and standard tiers in June 2026. Experiences now must match a tier on chat, random-reward purchases, ads, voice and data collection. Misclassified experiences lose tier-based discovery. Indonesia's ban also covers Roblox. Studios don't understand how classification works and brand clients fear child-privacy liability.
solution: A 'tier lint' tool that combines public metadata with scripted play-throughs to flag features that clash with each tier, gives a fix list (for example, disable free text in Kids, replace loot boxes) and produces a 'brand-safe by tier' report for sponsors. A public changelog tracks platform policy changes.
why_now: The tier split is only three months old and the rules are still moving. Toy and media brands (Mattel's games push, per the brief) are commissioning kids' UGC experiences, and state attorney-general suits against Roblox (from memory) raise brand caution.
revenue_model: Subscription at $500-3k a month per studio, plus $5-15k audits for brand-sponsored experiences.
non_obvious_insight: Tiering turns content rating into distribution: the platform's discovery algorithm becomes the regulator, and the UGC studio, not Roblox, eats the cost of getting it wrong. That is a classic compliance-consultancy niche, like Amazon seller-policy work.
first_30_days: Scrape metadata on the top 500 experiences. Identify about 30 likely mis-tiered ones. Send each studio owner a personalized mini-audit. Sell 10 audits at $1.5k. Start a public policy-change newsletter to build trust.
